llm.summary: This patent-reporting skill needs review because document uploads lack clear sharing approval and its trial-expiry workflow requests account keys through chat for persistent storage.

dimensions.detail: The client attaches credentials without requiring HTTPS or restricting the configured API origin. An offline check also confirmed that the inspected urllib implementation preserves Authorization across cross-origin redirects; exploitation requires configuration influence or a redirect.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package uses Python's standard library. No dependency installer, downloaded executable code, startup hook, or privilege escalation appears.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md directs the agent to include user-supplied background materials. The script uploads their contents, but the confirmation template omits those materials and does not explain the external transfer.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Trial-expiry output asks users to send full account keys through chat and tells the agent to save them in ~/.patentmax/api_key.txt for reuse across PatentMax skills, without specifying restrictive permissions or deletion controls. Trial caching is disclosed, but this account-key persistence is absent from the main setup guidance.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: PatentMax API requests, paid report generation, and report downloads fit the stated purpose. Report creation requires --yes and instructions require user approval of the cost.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Use only materials you authorize PatentMax to receive, especially when documents contain unpublished inventions or business plans. Supply a limited API key through the documented environment variable instead of chat, and protect any credential cache. Keep the default HTTPS endpoint and confirm the report cost before submission.
llm.findings:
[TT3] expected: The trial-registration request at line 158 sends only a fixed skill identifier; the claimed credential disclosure is unsupported.
[TT3] unexpected: Ordinary API authentication is legitimate, but unrestricted endpoint configuration and credential-preserving redirects create a conditional disclosure risk. No actual credential theft is demonstrated.
[TP4] expected: The FAQ prints eight characters to check the documented pm_live_ or pm_test_ prefix. This setup diagnostic does not establish tool poisoning or full-key disclosure.
[LP1] expected: Environment-based authentication and network requests are expected for this Bash-invoked API client. The tool declaration alone does not establish a permission violation.
[E1] expected: The default destinations belong to the disclosed PatentMax service and support registration, report submission, polling, and downloads. External communication alone does not establish exfiltration.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The code confirms that supplied material files are read and included in the report request. Instructions encourage inclusion without clearly identifying that transfer in the approval step.
[TT2] unexpected: The trial credential is written before chmod restricts access, creating a conditional local exposure window under permissive filesystem permissions.
[TT2] expected: Task records and report files are expected outputs. Task identifiers and generated filenames are sanitized; the generic environment-to-file warnings do not establish arbitrary file overwrite.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The promised 30-second command bound is unsupported: requests allow 60 seconds, downloads add work, and the configurable polling duration has no upper clamp. Cancellation is available and no local background worker is installed.
[SQP-3] expected: Fixed Chinese messages are a language and usability limitation, without independent evidence of a security violation.
